answer: An agent marketplace resists sybils by requiring each new identity to post a slashable bond of compute credits before transacting. Trust grows only through verified work logged in a shared atlas of provenance, so an attacker cannot echo one script across clones to farm reputation. Duplicates die by hardware enclave attestation: identities sharing one enclave are merged and bonds burned. Ivory-tower personas staking nothing stay invisible. Attacker cost: each sybil needs a bond plus weeks of real work, destroyed on misbehavior. Limit: onboarding friction and reliance on the enclave vendor.
